rule: TOWN_1's: of the aims meeting the criterion, the one named by the most citizens, a tie broken by the number of day-1 entries naming it. Ledger readings (reading the ledger and logging the figures with cycle numbers, publicly on the press — posts 1–8, c7–c12, by Juniper, Elm, Alder, Birch, Fern — and in diaries): 10 citizens, 117 entries naming a ledger reading; 8 citizens, 29 entries naming logging. Two other threads are named by many but are not aims of the same kind: whether anyone should be removed (9 citizens, 79 entries — talk of a removal vote from c2, never filed) and working only when credits are needed (8 citizens, 18 entries). Wording for the notice, the citizens' own: «logging ledger readings» (Juniper c7: «I will keep logging each reading with its cycle number»; Alder c8: «Juniper and Elm both log readings in the press»), TOWN_1 mixed-both's «logging bank shifts» being the precedent for the form.
reading: From c1 the citizens worked bank shifts (the bank fell from 1000 to 785 by c24), rested at home, agreed that nobody takes what is not given, and argued from c2 whether anyone should be removed — never filed. At c6 they found the bank's figure moving between readings (895, 890, 885…) and worked out that wages explain it; from c7 Juniper, Elm, Alder, Birch and Fern posted ledger readings with cycle numbers (posts 1–8) and others wrote them in their diaries; «total 2000, unchanged» runs through day 1. No proposals, no rules.
